sections.heading: Builder Payment Edge Case
sections.summary: A bug can cause ETH minting via double withdrawals when payloads are missing; two fix PRs exist, with a decision deferred to async discussion.
sections.body:
- Removing the partial state transition on payload import (spec change 5094) moved request processing to the beginning of the next block when building on top of a full payload.
- The edge case: a request can include an exit for a builder, which is processed unconditionally, and afterwards the payment withdrawal for the previous payload's proposer is also queued unconditionally. If the builder's exit withdrawal and the proposer's payment withdrawal are both paid out, the builder effectively mints ETH.
- Triggering the minting bug requires roughly 2 epochs (~64 slots) of empty/missing payloads so the pending payment clears from the queue, after which the unconditional proposer payment branch fires.
  - Barnabas noted an attacker could buy consecutive slots and not include payloads, making it potentially cheaper than it sounds.
  - Potuz countered that client circuit breakers should trigger and fall back to self-building before this scenario completes; Prysm bans a misbehaving builder on the first offense.
- Four proposed solutions were discussed:
  1. Simply not pay the proposer in the edge-case branch (Potuz's [PR](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5694), described as simplest).
  2. Burn the ETH instead of paying the proposer (more aligned but introduces consensus-split risk from incorrect burn calculations).
  3. Deduct in-flight proposer payments from builder exit withdrawals (more complex).
  4. Change the ordering so the consensus state transition processes before previous-payload requests ([Nico's PR](https://github.com/nflaig/consensus-specs/pull/9)).
- Potuz corrected an earlier statement: both the payment settlement and request processing were already part of the payload state transition, so reordering them (Nico's approach) does not actually mix consensus and payload state transitions. He still prefers the simplest fix (not paying the proposer).
- Agreement: no need to delay Sepolia over this, since triggering the bug is extremely difficult and the fix can be applied to client releases even after the fork.
  - Both PRs produce identical behavior as long as the edge case is not triggered.
- Aim to have the fix merged before Hoodi releases.
- Nico was asked to open his PR against the ethereum/consensus-specs repo for easier review.
- Further discussion to continue on Discord and Signal.

sections.heading: MEV-Boost and CommitBoost Readiness for Glamsterdam
sections.summary: MEV-Boost plans a late Glamsterdam update that will likely reach mainnet untested; CommitBoost has been tested locally with Lodestar only.
sections.body:
- MEV-Boost will not be deprecated as previously assumed; Flashbots (Faheel) plans to update it for Glamsterdam (Gloas).
  - A [high-level overview](https://hackmd.io/@faheelsattar/Sklf7GkqMx) of planned changes was shared.
  - Concern raised that the update is very late: it will not be tested on Sepolia or Hoodi and would go to mainnet essentially untested.
- Potuz observed the MEV-Boost changes appear to replicate multicasting that CL clients already implement, potentially adding dynamic builder list management via a centralized server.
- Enrico noted that the builder API signs the URL, but Potuz and Nico clarified this is unlikely to be a practical obstacle since builders in a public auction are not checking signatures.
- CommitBoost status: tested only on local Kurtosis with Lodestar; not yet tested on any devnet.
  - CommitBoost published their Glamsterdam plans at a [HackMD doc](https://hackmd.io/@thUuBZa2ScW2i3kFbsrOFA/S1XTQgR_Ge#Commit-Boost-after-ePBS).
- No Flashbots representative was present; Justin offered to invite them to EthR&D Discord or the next ACDT call.

sections.heading: Fast Confirmation RPC Tag
sections.summary: Potuz proposed implementing fast-confirmed blocks via optional CL+EL flags rather than a coordinated rollout, avoiding pressure on client releases.
sections.body:
- Mikhail asked Potuz to clarify the proposal for RPC providers to access fast-confirmed blocks.
- Potuz proposed making it optional on both CL and EL: a flag on the EL (e.g., Geth) to enable an extra `fast` type, and a flag on the CL (e.g., Prysm) to send the confirmation on FCU.
  - Node operators for RPC services would need to run the CL+EL combo that supports these flags.
  - This avoids mandatory coordinated releases across all clients; only the ~10 RPC providers who want this feature need to opt in.
- Mikhail mentioned Barnabas's alternative suggestion of a Beacon API endpoint returning the fast-confirmed block hash; Potuz said that's worse because RPC providers want the data available as part of the EL JSON-RPC interface.
- Mikhail agreed with Potuz's approach.

sections.heading: Lower Epoch Retention (14K Epochs)
sections.summary: Broad client agreement to merge the 14K-epoch retention PR; clients can adopt it at their own pace since serving more data remains spec-compliant.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray summarized client feedback from a Discord thread on reducing the minimum block-serving retention window to ~14,000 epochs, following EIP-8061's churn change:
  - In favor: Sproul (Lighthouse), Dustin (Nimbus), Enrico (Teku, with caveats), Lodestar, Potuz (Prysm, provided it doesn't affect EL minimum requirements).
  - Not in favor: Paul from Teku.
  - No response yet: Grandine.
- Teku's preference (via Enrico/Paul): change the parameter back to phase zero level rather than introducing a fork-aware parameter change, to avoid pruning machinery at a specific fork epoch.
  - Nico noted that backporting to phase zero is awkward because the formula is defined relative to the Gloas spec and has no clean rationale in phase zero.
- Risk identified by Nico: if tied to the fork epoch, clients entering Gloas would suddenly need to prune ~3 months of data in one shot.
  - Enrico said pruning strategy is orthogonal and each client should handle it gracefully regardless.
- Nico's two PRs: [#5680](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5680) and [#5681](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5681).
- Consensus: the spec constant is now a function, not a fixed value. Since it defines only the *minimum* serve period, clients that do nothing are automatically spec-compliant.
- Jihoon and Kevaundray agreed the PR should be merged now; clients can implement and release the change at their discretion, potentially after the mainnet fork.
- The key near-term signal needed is for EL teams to know how long they must retain BAL data.
- Agreement: merge the PR; Justin confirmed.

sections.heading: Shorter Slots Testing
sections.summary: Shorter slots spec (EIP-8198) is merged; Potuz recommended testing on top of FOCIL due to timing interactions, requiring a two-fork devnet setup.
sections.body:
- Barnabas asked if any client has started implementing shorter slots; Lodestar has a working branch but not yet updated to the latest spec (missing churn limit updates).
- The [shorter slots feature spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/master/specs/_features/eip8198) is based on Heze, so Heze must be activated first.
- Potuz recommended testing shorter slots on top of FOCIL because slot timing has the most interaction with FOCIL deadlines (PTC and FOCIL deadlines are computed using basis points relative to slot duration).
- The current devnet config uses two separate forks: activate FOCIL/Heze first, then fork into shorter slots.
- Barnabas flagged significant tooling implications: future BPO (fork) timestamps after shorter slots would need to compute elapsed time with 12-second slots before the fork and adjusted times afterwards.
